name: Tabimorelin
summary: Early experimental oral GH secretagogue; a few early human studies and no appearance data.
lead: Tabimorelin (NN703) is an experimental, orally active growth hormone secretagogue that was among the earlier compounds in its class. It acts on the ghrelin receptor to stimulate growth hormone release.

name: GHRP-1
summary: Early research growth hormone releasing peptide; some 1990s human data and no appearance evidence.
lead: GHRP-1 (growth hormone releasing peptide-1) is a synthetic peptide from the first family of growth hormone releasing peptides, which also includes GHRP-6 and GHRP-2. These small peptides of six to seven amino acids stimulate growth hormone release through a receptor distinct from the GHRH receptor.

name: Alexamorelin
summary: An obscure hexarelin-related GH secretagogue peptide known mostly from anti-doping screening papers; no appearance trials exist.
lead: Alexamorelin is a synthetic heptapeptide growth hormone secretagogue, related to hexarelin, with the sequence Ala-His-D-2-methyl-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2. A 2000 study reported its endocrine activities in humans .

name: Deslorelin
summary: A veterinary GnRH-agonist implant with some pediatric endocrine research; nothing tests it for looks.
lead: Deslorelin is a synthetic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) superagonist used mainly in veterinary medicine, sold under names such as Suprelorin, Ovuplant and Sucromate Equine . It is used to control reproduction in animals, for example to induce ovulation in mares and as a slow-release implant for reversible contraception in dogs and ferrets .

name: Ganirelix
summary: A GnRH-antagonist fertility drug for IVF; its place on a looks list rests on hormone suppression, not any appearance trial.
lead: Ganirelix, sold as Orgalutran and Antagon among other names, is an injectable GnRH antagonist used in assisted reproduction to prevent premature ovulation during ovarian stimulation for IVF . It competitively blocks pituitary GnRH receptors, rapidly suppressing LH and FSH, with the effect reversing after stopping .

name: Humanin
summary: A mitochondria-derived peptide with cell and animal research behind it, and no human trials as a treatment.
lead: Humanin is a short peptide encoded within mitochondrial DNA, in the gene for 16S ribosomal RNA, and was the first mitochondria-derived peptide identified . It was discovered in 2001 by several groups studying different questions, including protection of neurons against Alzheimer-related toxicity , interaction with the apoptosis protein Bax  and with IGFBP-3 .

name: Dihexa
summary: An experimental angiotensin IV-derived peptide studied in rodents for memory; it has no published human trials and no link to appearance.
lead: Dihexa is a synthetic oligopeptide analog of angiotensin IV, modified to be more stable and to penetrate the brain . It emerged from work on angiotensin IV analogs as potential antidementia agents .

name: Selank
summary: A Russian-developed anxiolytic peptide that forum users group with Semax as a nootropic; human evidence is limited to a few Russian-language studies.
lead: Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) designed as a longer-lasting analog of tuftsin, a tetrapeptide fragment of immunoglobulin G. It was developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences together with the Zakusov Institute of Pharmacology .
claims: Selank and Semax are useful nootropics for focus and mood.

name: Cerebrolysin
summary: A porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved for stroke and dementia in many countries, discussed by forum users as an "iqmaxxing" nootropic.
lead: Cerebrolysin is a mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and free amino acids produced by enzymatic breakdown of porcine brain proteins, described as mimicking neurotrophic factors . It is manufactured by EVER Neuro Pharma in Austria and given by injection or infusion .
claims: Cerebrolysin boosts intelligence and study performance ("iqmaxxing").
It supports brain recovery and neurogenesis.

name: Noopept (Omberacetam)
summary: A Russian-developed racetam-like nootropic with small human studies and no appearance evidence.
lead: Noopept, also called omberacetam or GVS-111, is a synthetic dipeptide-like compound promoted as a nootropic (cognitive enhancer). Chemically it is N-phenylacetyl-L-prolylglycine ethyl ester, and it is described as a prodrug of the endogenous dipeptide cycloprolylglycine; it is related to the racetam family. It was developed by Russian pharmacology researchers, including T. A. Gudasheva and S. B. Seredenin, and its synthesis was first reported in 1996.

name: Coluracetam
summary: An abandoned pharma racetam sold as a nootropic, with no appearance evidence.
lead: Coluracetam (also MKC-231 or BCI-540) is an experimental racetam-class compound promoted as a nootropic. It was developed by Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma, first for Alzheimer's disease, and later licensed to BrainCells Inc. for major depressive disorder and comorbid anxiety. It is not approved anywhere.

name: Fasoracetam
summary: A never-marketed racetam studied for ADHD, with no appearance evidence.
lead: Fasoracetam is an experimental racetam-class drug discovered by Nippon Shinyaku in the late 1980s and never marketed. It was tested for vascular dementia, then repurposed for ADHD and later other conditions. It appears to modulate metabotropic glutamate receptors.

name: Nefiracetam
summary: A Japanese racetam studied for dementia and post-stroke apathy, with no appearance evidence.
lead: Nefiracetam (code DM-9384) is an oral racetam-class nootropic studied mainly in Japan for dementia and post-stroke apathy. It is not approved in the United States, where it is unscheduled, and it is prescription-only in Australia.

name: Sunifiram
summary: An unapproved animal-tested nootropic with no human trials and no appearance evidence.
lead: Sunifiram (DM-235) is an experimental nootropic from a series of piperazine compounds made by Italian researchers; it is a structural simplification of unifiram (DM-232). In animal studies it showed antiamnesic effects at much lower doses than piracetam. It has not been approved anywhere.

name: Unifiram
summary: An unapproved animal-tested nootropic with no human studies and no appearance evidence.
lead: Unifiram (DM-232) is an experimental compound that showed antiamnesic effects in animal studies, with far greater potency than piracetam. It was developed by Italian researchers and is the parent of sunifiram. It is not patented and is sold online despite the absence of human and long-term toxicity studies.

name: Modafinil
summary: Prescription wakefulness drug that forums treat as a study and productivity aid; no appearance effect has been studied.
lead: Modafinil is a prescription wakefulness-promoting medication, often grouped as a eugeroic, that the US Food and Drug Administration has approved to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea or shift work disorder . It was developed in France by Laboratoire Lafon and is described as a related compound to adrafinil .
claims: Modafinil makes users more alert, productive and focused without the jitters of caffeine.
Modafinil helps appearance, for example by raising charisma or social ability.

name: Armodafinil
summary: The longer-acting R-enantiomer of modafinil, prescribed for sleepiness; no appearance effect has been studied.
lead: Armodafinil is the R-enantiomer of modafinil and a prescription wakefulness-promoting medication. The US label lists it to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness associated with obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy or shift work disorder, and specifies that in sleep apnea it treats sleepiness and not the underlying obstruction . Grokipedia gives the brand name as Nuvigil and a 2007 US approval .

name: Adrafinil
summary: A modafinil prodrug once sold in France; no appearance use has been studied and human data are thin.
lead: Adrafinil is a wakefulness-promoting compound that the body converts to modafinil. According to Grokipedia, it was developed by Laboratoire Lafon in France, marketed there as Olmifon from the mid-1980s for vigilance problems in older adults, and withdrawn by its manufacturer in 2011 .

name: Citicoline (CDP-choline)
summary: A choline-donor nootropic studied for stroke and brain injury; no trial tests it for appearance.
lead: Citicoline, or cytidine 5'-diphosphocholine (CDP-choline), is a nucleotide that occurs naturally in the body as an intermediate in the synthesis of phosphatidylcholine, a membrane phospholipid . It is sold as a prescription drug in some countries for stroke and cognitive disorders and as a dietary supplement in others, including the United States, according to Grokipedia .

name: Alpha-GPC
summary: A choline donor sold as a cognitive and sports supplement; no appearance outcome has been studied.
lead: Alpha-GPC (L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine, or choline alfoscerate) is a choline-containing compound that serves as a source of choline for the synthesis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine and for cell membrane phospholipids . According to Grokipedia, it is a prescription drug in some countries such as Italy for cognitive decline and is sold as a dietary supplement in the United States, where a 2012 GRAS notice addressed its use as a choline source .

name: Huperzine A
summary: Club-moss cholinesterase inhibitor sold as a nootropic and floated in height-maxxing; no height study exists.
lead: Huperzine A is a plant alkaloid isolated from the Chinese club moss Huperzia serrata and a potent, reversible inhibitor of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase, which breaks down acetylcholine . Grokipedia states that it has been approved as a prescription drug for Alzheimer's disease in China since 1996 and is sold elsewhere as a dietary supplement .
claims: Huperzine A is a somatostatin inhibitor that raises growth hormone and could add height.
The somatostatin claim is a mix-up with pyridostigmine, so huperzine A does nothing for height.
Raising acetylcholine indirectly lowers somatostatin and so could raise growth hormone.

name: Bacopa monnieri
summary: Ayurvedic "brahmi" herb sold as a memory nootropic; trials are small and reviews call the evidence for cognition inconclusive.
lead: Bacopa monnieri, known as brahmi or water hyssop, is a creeping perennial herb of tropical and subtropical wetlands that is used in Ayurvedic medicine, where it has traditionally been associated with memory and learning. Its best-characterised constituents are the bacosides, a family of dammarane-type triterpenoid saponins.

name: Ginkgo biloba
summary: Leaf extract of the ancient ginkgo tree sold as a memory and circulation supplement; large reviews find no conclusive benefit and it carries bleeding-interaction cautions.
lead: Ginkgo biloba, the ginkgo or maidenhair tree, is a long-lived deciduous tree native to China and the only living species in its division. Standardised leaf extracts are sold as supplements and, in some European countries, as herbal medicines for cognitive complaints.

name: Vinpocetine
summary: Semi-synthetic periwinkle derivative sold in Europe as a prescription drug and in the US as a supplement; evidence for benefit in dementia or stroke is described as unsupported by full reviews, and the FDA warns about pregnancy.
lead: Vinpocetine (ethyl apovincaminate) is a synthetic derivative of the vinca alkaloid vincamine, extracted from lesser periwinkle (Vinca minor) or Voacanga africana seeds. Grokipedia (AI-generated) describes it as developed by the Hungarian company Gedeon Richter and marketed in Hungary as Cavinton from 1978.

name: Sulbutiamine
summary: Lipid-soluble thiamine (B1) derivative prescribed for fatigue in France and sold elsewhere as a supplement; human data are sparse.
lead: Sulbutiamine (isobutyrylthiamine disulfide) is a synthetic, lipophilic derivative of thiamine in which two thiamine molecules are linked by a disulfide bridge. Servier marketed it in France from 1973 as Arcalion, and it is prescribed there for asthenia.

name: Pyritinol
summary: Vitamin B6 disulfide analog approved in several European countries for dementia-related impairment and sold as a US nootropic supplement; evidence is dated and mixed.
lead: Pyritinol, also called pyrithioxine or pyridoxine disulfide, is a semi-synthetic water-soluble analog of vitamin B6 first produced by Merck in 1961. From the 1970s it was sold as a prescription and over-the-counter drug in several countries, and since the early 1990s as a nootropic supplement in the United States.

name: Meclofenoxate (Centrophenoxine)
summary: DMAE ester nootropic with 1970s elderly-memory studies and a mouse-lifespan claim behind its "anti-aging" reputation; no studies of skin.
lead: Meclofenoxate, also called centrophenoxine, is an ester of dimethylethanolamine (DMAE) and 4-chlorophenoxyacetic acid. It is sold as a prescription drug in Japan and some European countries including Germany, Hungary and Austria, and as a supplement elsewhere.

name: Bromantane
summary: Russian adamantane stimulant-anxiolytic traded as a motivation nootropic; human data are small and mostly Russian-language.
lead: Bromantane (also spelled bromantan; Russian brand name Ladasten) is a synthetic adamantane derivative, chemically N-(4-bromophenyl)adamantan-2-amine, that is related to amantadine and memantine. It is described in the literature as an atypical stimulant and anxiolytic and as an "actoprotector", a term used in Russian pharmacology for synthetic adaptogens said to raise resistance to physical and psychological stress.
claims: Bromantane raises baseline dopamine and motivation
It lowers anxiety and social stress
It boosts testosterone and lowers prolactin, aiding physique
It resensitises users to stimulants such as caffeine or methylphenidate

name: Phosphatidylserine
summary: Membrane phospholipid sold as a memory and recovery supplement; trials are mainly in cognition, none for appearance.
lead: Phosphatidylserine (PS) is a glycerophospholipid found in all cell membranes, most abundant in the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane and enriched in the brain, where it makes up roughly 13 to 15 percent of cortical phospholipids.  It is also sold as an oral dietary supplement, usually derived from soy lecithin, marketed for memory and cognition, and in sports and recovery products for exercise stress.

name: Dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE)
summary: Industrial amino alcohol used in skin-firming creams and sold as a nootropic; no human trial isolates its skin effect.
lead: Dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE, also dimethylethanolamine, DMEA or deanol) is a colourless amino alcohol with the formula (CH3)2NCH2CH2OH. It is mainly an industrial chemical, used as a curing agent for polyurethanes and epoxy resins and as an intermediate for other compounds.
